hero.tagline: Where starlight whispers through the swirling firmament

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Chandra's ancient light upon the tide
moon.intro: Selene, the Greek Titaness of the Moon, drove her silver chariot across the night sky, illuminating the world with borrowed light — a reminder that even reflection can be a form of brilliance.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: The ego: dust that thinks itself a mountain
philosophy.intro: True art requires the death of the ego. The painter who paints for fame paints nothing true. The musician who plays for applause hears nothing real. Creation begins where the self ends.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: The garment worn for a season, then cast off
gita.intro: The Bhagavad Gita begins not with wisdom but with despair. Arjuna, the greatest warrior, drops his bow and says, 'I will not fight.' The scripture teaches that the darkest moment precedes the greatest clarity.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Between two eternities of stillness, the dance
shiva.intro: The Shiv Purana describes the damaru — Shiva's drum — as the source of all language and music. The first sound, Nada, is the vibration from which all creation emerges. Music is not entertainment; it is cosmology.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: The alchemy of perception: making the invisible seen
art.intro: Waves are the ocean's way of communicating with the shore. Each one is unique, yet all are the same water. Identity is like a wave — real in its moment, eternal in its substance.
